9: 
10: # create-diff
11: 
12: > Capture what changed in an edited document, offline, without Git, as one HTML report you can open in any browser.
13: 
14: ---
15: 
16: ## 1. AT A GLANCE
17: 
18: | Aspect | What you get |
19: |---|---|
20: | **Use it for** | Reviewing what changed in a locally edited Markdown, text, HTML, DOCX or text-PDF document without Git |
21: | **Invoke with** | `python3 scripts/create_diff.py snapshot / compare / compare-pair` or `/create:diff` |
22: | **Works on** | One document at a time or a pre-composed multi-file aggregate pair |
23: | **Produces** | A single self-contained HTML report with inlined CSS, zero JavaScript, no remote references and no network calls |
24: 
25: ---
26: 
27: ## 2. OVERVIEW
28: 
29: ### Why This Skill Exists
30: 
31: Not everything you edit lives in Git. An AI or a person edits a Markdown spec, a DOCX brief, a PDF export or a text file outside version control and now needs to know exactly what changed before trusting it. Diffing that by eye is unreliable beyond a sentence. Pasting the file into a hosted diff tool sends its content somewhere you may not want it to go. create-diff exists so review works the same everywhere: local and offline, never touching the source file.
32: 
33: ### What It Does
34: 
35: create-diff captures a baseline snapshot of a document before an edit happens, then compares the current file against that snapshot or an explicit second file and renders one self-contained HTML report you can open offline. The engine ships as `scripts/create_diff.py` and reads Markdown, plain text, HTML, DOCX and text-layer PDF. It does not touch code or Git-tracked files: that boundary belongs to `sk-git`. It does not audit a single document on its own either, since comparing two states is the point. `create-quality-control` handles single-document scoring.
36: 
37: ### The Format Fidelity Layer
38: 
39: Every comparison runs at a stated fidelity tier so a limited result is never mistaken for a complete one. The engine extracts what a format can honestly give:
40: 
41: | Format | What the skill knows how to operate |
42: |---|---|
43: | **Plain text** | diff `.txt`, `.log`, `.csv` and unknown text-like files at full fidelity after normalization |
44: | **Markdown** | diff `.md`, `.markdown` and `.mdown` files at full fidelity, comparing normalized text with rendered HTML left out |
45: | **HTML** | extract visible text and `h1` to `h6` headings at text fidelity, with CSS and scripts left out |
46: | **DOCX** | compare paragraph text, table text and heading-styled paragraphs at text fidelity |
47: | **PDF** | diff the extracted text layer at `text*` fidelity when a local extractor is installed, with scanned pages warned and OCR out of scope |
48: 
49: ---
50: 
51: ## 3. QUICK START
52: 
53: **Step 1: capture a baseline before the edit.**
54: 
55: ```bash
56: python3 scripts/create_diff.py snapshot path/to/doc.md
57: ```
58: 
59: Confirms a snapshot was stored. Nothing else changes.
60: 
61: **Step 2: after the edit, compare and render.**
62: 
63: ```bash
64: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare path/to/doc.md --report review.html
65: ```
66: 
67: Or, without a stored baseline, compare two explicit files directly using the shipped fixtures:
68: 
69: ```bash
70: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare-pair \
71:   --before assets/fixtures/onboarding-before.md \
72:   --after  assets/fixtures/onboarding-after.md \
73:   --report /tmp/onboarding-review.html
74: ```
75: 
76: You get one HTML file with a change summary line like `markdown, tier full, +6 -0 ~3` and a unified or side-by-side diff view.
77: 
78: **Step 3: verify the report before you hand it off.**
79: 
80: ```bash
81: python3 scripts/validate_report.py /tmp/onboarding-review.html
82: ```
83: 
84: Prints `PASS` when the report is safe and self-contained.
85: 
86: ---
87: 
88: ## 4. HOW IT WORKS
89: 
90: The lifecycle has one hard invariant: the baseline has to exist before the edit happens. `snapshot` copies the current file into a local `.create-diff/` store without altering the source. Once the edit is done, `compare` diffs the live file against its latest stored baseline and writes the report. When no baseline exists or you already have two explicit versions, `compare-pair` skips the store entirely and diffs `--before` against `--after`. Either path ends the same way: a deterministic line-and-word diff, run through a format-aware extractor and rendered into one inlined-CSS HTML file with no scripts and no network calls.
91: 
92: ### Key Concept: Aggregate File Boundaries
93: 
94: `compare-pair` can also review a bundle of files in one call, as long as both `--before` and `--after` wrap every file in matching `===== BEGIN FILE: <path> =====` and `===== END FILE: <path> =====` markers. When the markers line up, the report renders each transition as a full-width boundary band with a canvas gap before it, so a five-file bundle still reads as five distinct reviews instead of one file's heading bleeding into the next. Malformed or unbalanced markers just render as ordinary text. The CLI itself still only ever receives one before-document and one after-document.
95: 
96: ---
97: 
98: ## 5. INTEGRATION & NAVIGATION
99: 
100: ### When To Use This Skill
101: 
102: Reach for create-diff when an AI or a person edited a document outside Git and you need proof of what changed, when you want a baseline captured before a risky edit or when a pre-composed multi-file bundle needs its transitions to stay visible in review. Skip it for code or anything already tracked in Git (`sk-git` owns that). Skip it for visual or pixel-level comparison (out of scope: create-diff compares extracted text only). Skip it for scoring a single document with no second state to compare (`create-quality-control` owns that).
103: 
104: ### Related Skills
105: 
106: | Skill | Relationship |
107: |---|---|
108: | `sk-git` | Owns diffs for code and Git-tracked files. create-diff is for everything outside that boundary. |
109: | Visual / pixel-level comparison | Out of scope: create-diff only compares extracted text. |
110: | `create-quality-control` | Audits one existing document. create-diff always compares two states. |
111: 
112: ---
113: 
114: ## 6. TROUBLESHOOTING
115: 
116: | What you see | Why | Fix |
117: |---|---|---|
118: | Exit `4`, missing baseline | `compare` ran with no stored snapshot for that file | Run `snapshot` first or use `compare-pair` with explicit `--before` and `--after` |
119: | Exit `3`, unsupported format | The file type has no extractor or the PDF has no text layer | Run `capabilities` to see what is available or provide a pre-extracted explicit pair |
120: | Report already exists | The engine refuses to overwrite an existing report path | Pass a new `--report` path or remove the old file first |
121: | File-boundary bands missing on a multi-file pair | The `BEGIN FILE` and `END FILE` markers are unbalanced or unmatched between the two inputs | Match marker order and paths exactly in both `--before` and `--after` |
122: | `validate_report.py` fails | The report references a remote resource or an inline script somehow made it through | Fix the renderer input and regenerate. Never hand off a failed report as clean |
123: 
124: ---
125: 
126: ## 7. FAQ
127: 
128: **Q: Why not just use `git diff` for this?**
129: 
130: A: Git needs the file under version control with commit history. create-diff works on any document, anywhere on disk, without ever needing a Git repo.
131: 
132: **Q: Does this send my document anywhere?**
133: 
134: A: No. Everything runs locally with the Python standard library. The report has no scripts and no remote references. When PDF extraction is available it uses a local extractor only.
135: 
136: **Q: What if the document is a scanned PDF?**
137: 
138: A: There is no text layer to diff, so the comparison would be empty. OCR is out of scope. Use the explicit-pair fallback with pre-extracted text instead.
139: 
140: **Q: Can I compare more than two files at once?**
141: 
142: A: `compare-pair` accepts one before-document and one after-document, but you can pre-compose either side into a multi-file bundle using the `BEGIN FILE` and `END FILE` markers described in Section 4.
143: 
144: ---
145: 
146: ## 8. VERIFICATION
147: 
148: | Check | Result |
149: |---|---|
150: | `python3 scripts/validate_report.py <report>` | `PASS` (asserts doctype, `lang`, a CSP meta tag, zero `<script>`, no inline handlers and no remote resources) |
151: | Source unchanged | The source file stays byte-for-byte identical before and after `compare` or `compare-pair` |
152: | Manual scenarios | `manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md` groups scenarios by snapshot lifecycle, comparison formats and safety guarantees |
153: 
154: ---
155: 
156: ## 9. RELATED DOCUMENTS
157: 
158: | Document | Purpose |
159: |---|---|
160: | [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md) | Authoritative packet contract and rules |
161: | [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) | Machine router: intent map, resource map and loading levels |
162: | [`references/README.md`](./references/README.md) | Reference route-map |
163: | [`references/cli-reference.md`](./references/cli-reference.md) | Full command, flag and exit-code reference |
164: | [`references/capabilities-and-fidelity.md`](./references/capabilities-and-fidelity.md) | Format support matrix and fidelity tiers |
165: | [`references/workflow.md`](./references/workflow.md) | Baseline, explicit-pair and snapshot lifecycle |
166: | [`references/accessibility-contract.md`](./references/accessibility-contract.md) | The report's accessibility guarantees |
167: | [`assets/fixtures/README.md`](./assets/fixtures/README.md) | Runnable before/after worked example |
168: | [`feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md`](./feature-catalog/feature-catalog.md) | Canonical capability inventory |
169: | [`manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md`](./manual-testing-playbook/manual-testing-playbook.md) | Operator-facing validation scenarios |

8: # Create Diff
9: 
10: `create-diff` is the `sk-doc` workflow packet for reviewing what changed in a locally edited document.
11: It works outside Git and without a hosted service.
12: It captures a baseline before an edit, compares the before and after versions, then renders one self-contained, accessible HTML report.
13: The comparison engine ships with this packet as `scripts/create_diff.py`.
14: Everything runs on the machine: no network, no upload and no telemetry, and source files are never modified.

22: ## 1. WHEN TO USE
23: 
24: ### Activation Triggers
25: 
26: Use this packet when the request asks to:
27: 
28: - Review what an AI (or anyone) changed in a locally edited document.
29: - Produce a before/after report for a Markdown, text, HTML, DOCX, or PDF file that is not in Git.
30: - Capture a baseline of a document before editing it, so the change can be reviewed afterward.
31: - Compare two explicit versions of a document (an old file and a new file).
32: 
33: Keyword triggers: `create diff report`, `document before/after review`, `before/after document diff`, `document change report`, `review document edits`, `docx diff`, `pdf diff`.
34: 
35: ### When NOT to Use
36: 
37: Route elsewhere when:
38: 
39: - The files are code or already tracked in Git — use `git`/`sk-git` for source diffs.
40: - The comparison is visual or design-oriented (layout, pixels, screenshots) — out of scope; create-diff compares extracted text only.
41: - The task is auditing, scoring, or validating a single existing document rather than comparing two states — use `create-quality-control`.
42: - The deliverable is a README, skill, command, agent, changelog, or flowchart — use the matching `create-*` packet.
43: 
44: If the target document or output path is unknown and acting would be a guess, ask before writing.
45:

47: 
48: ## 2. SMART ROUTING
49: 
50: The `sk-doc` hub resolves a document before/after review through `mode-registry.json`.
51: `hub-router.json` scores the request, the winning `workflowMode` is `sk-create-diff`, and the hub loads this `SKILL.md` first.
52: A request to review what an AI or a person changed in a locally edited document, to capture a baseline before an edit or to compare two explicit versions selects this packet.
53: Two shapes exist: an automatic snapshot-backed baseline and an explicit pair.
54: The comparison reads extracted text only, so a visual or design comparison is out of scope.
55: 
56: `references/README.md` is the route map and the fallback load, and `references/cli-reference.md` holds the commands and exit codes.
57: 
58: A request that matches no registered mode returns `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK`, never a silent default.
59: 
60: Read [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md) before selecting skill-local resources; open only the matched files.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## 3. HOW IT WORKS
65: 
66: All comparison, extraction, snapshotting, and rendering are done by `scripts/create_diff.py`. Run it from this packet directory (or give an absolute path to it). The invariant is: **capture the baseline before the edit** — a diff needs a real before-state.
67: 
68: ### Automatic flow (snapshot-backed)
69: 
70: ```bash
71: # 0. (optional) confirm what is supported and at what fidelity
72: python3 scripts/create_diff.py capabilities
73: 
74: # 1. BEFORE the edit — capture a baseline (copies the file into a local .create-diff/ store;
75: #    never touches the source)
76: python3 scripts/create_diff.py snapshot path/to/doc.md
77: 
78: # 2. ... let the edit happen (AI or human) ...
79: 
80: # 3. AFTER the edit — compare the current file against its latest baseline and render the report
81: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare path/to/doc.md --report review.html
82: ```
83: 
84: ### Explicit-pair flow (fallback — no stored state needed)
85: 
86: Use this when there is no baseline, when comparing two arbitrary versions, or when the automatic store is unavailable:
87: 
88: ```bash
89: python3 scripts/create_diff.py compare-pair --before old.md --after new.md --report review.html
90: ```
91: 
92: ### Pre-composed aggregate pairs
93: 
94: `compare-pair` can also review a pre-composed pair containing two or more files.
95: Wrap every file in both inputs with the same ordered, unique markers:
96: 
97: ```text
98: ===== BEGIN FILE: docs/first.md =====
99: [file content]
100: ===== END FILE: docs/first.md =====
101: ===== BEGIN FILE: docs/second.md =====
102: [file content]
103: ===== END FILE: docs/second.md =====
104: ```
105: 
106: When both inputs contain a balanced matching envelope, the report renders every
107: start and end as an explicit full-width boundary band. Boundaries stay visible
108: through collapsed context, later files receive a 32px canvas gap before their

17: link that points here; this file holds the declaration a reader parses to decide what loads.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: Requests reach this packet when the ask is to review what an AI or a person changed in a locally
24: edited document, to capture a baseline before an edit, or to compare two explicit versions of a
25: document that is not in Git — Markdown, text, HTML, DOCX or a text-layer PDF. It routes to three
26: resource families: the reference set under `references/`, which starts at `references/README.md` and
27: extends to the CLI, capability-and-fidelity, workflow, accessibility-contract and worked-example
28: documents; the worked-example fixtures under `assets/`; and the two packet scripts,
29: `scripts/create_diff.py` and `scripts/validate_report.py`, which carry the comparison and the report
30: check themselves. A visual or design comparison, and any code or Git diff, is out of scope and
31: routes to another packet.
32: 
33: The router answers one question: given a request, which skill-local resources load, in what order, and
34: what happens when nothing matches. Every path below stays inside this skill folder, and no resource
35: loads before an intent selects it.
36: 
37: ---
38:

40:

42: - **`explicit_pair`** — "compare two files", "old and new", "before and after files" or "explicit pair" fires it at weight 4, and it needs no stored state: two explicit versions go straight into `compare-pair`. It loads the same discovered inventory as the intent above, for the same reason, and `references/README.md` is again the default resource.
43: 
44: ---

49: reader finds it. This section is the last in the file, and it holds the only pseudocode.

14: # Capabilities & fidelity tiers
15: 
16: ## 1. OVERVIEW
17: 
18: A diff is only as trustworthy as the extraction behind it. `create-diff` tells the user what tier a comparison is at, so a limited result is never mistaken for a complete one. Run `python3 ../scripts/create_diff.py capabilities` (from the packet dir) to see the live matrix and which PDF extractor, if any, is available.
19: 
20: ---
21: 
22: ## 2. TIERS
23: 
24: | Tier | Meaning |
25: | --- | --- |
26: | `full` | Highest-fidelity text comparison — after the normalization described below (Unicode NFC, line endings, per-line trailing whitespace). |
27: | `text` | Visible/structural text only; formatting, styling, and non-text content are not compared. |
28: | `text*` | Text layer only, and only when an optional extractor is installed. |
29: | `unsupported` | No reliable local extraction available. |
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 3. FORMAT MATRIX
34: 
35: | Format | Extensions | Tier | Compared | Not compared |
36: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
37: | text | `.txt`, `.text`, `.log`, `.csv`, unknown text-like | `full` | text (after normalization) | trailing whitespace, line-ending style, a final newline, Unicode form |
38: | markdown | `.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown` | `full` | text (after normalization) | rendered-HTML output; heading/section structure |
39: | html | `.html`, `.htm`, `.xhtml` | `text` | visible text, `<h1>`–`<h6>` headings | CSS, attributes, inline styles, `<script>`/`<style>` content, layout |
40: | docx | `.docx` | `text` | paragraph and table text, heading-styled paragraphs | run formatting, styles, images, comments, tracked changes |
41: | pdf | `.pdf` | `text*` | extracted text layer | layout, fonts, images; scanned/image-only pages |
42: 
43: Unknown *text-like* extensions are treated as plain text, and the report carries a fidelity warning saying so, so the assumption can be corrected. Known binary or unsupported extensions — spreadsheets, presentations, images, and archives (`.xlsx`, `.pptx`, `.png`, `.zip`, …) — are refused with exit `3` rather than raw-byte "text"-diffed into a meaningless report. An *unknown* extension whose first 8 KB contains a NUL byte is treated as binary and refused the same way. A file that is not valid UTF-8 is likewise refused with exit `3` rather than decoded with replacement characters (`�`): silent replacement can make two files that differ only in undecodable bytes look identical, hiding a real difference.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ## 4. PDF DEPENDENCY
48: 
49: Text-PDF support needs one local extractor, probed in this order:
50: 
51: 1. **`pdftotext`** (poppler) — on `PATH`. On macOS: `brew install poppler`.
52: 2. **`pypdf`** — `pip install pypdf`.
53: 3. **`pdfplumber`** — `pip install pdfplumber`.
54: 
55: If none is present, `compare`/`compare-pair` on a PDF exits `3` with an actionable message. The fallback is to extract the text yourself and run `compare-pair --before old.txt --after new.txt`.
56: 
57: ---
58: 
59: ## 5. SCANNED PDFS
60: 
61: A PDF with no text layer (a scan/image) extracts to empty text. The engine detects this and adds a prominent warning to the report rather than presenting an empty, misleading diff. OCR is deliberately out of scope for this mode.
62: 
63: ---
64: 
65: ## 6. NORMALIZATION
66: 
67: Before diffing, both sides are canonicalized so incidental encoding differences are not reported as edits: Unicode NFC, `\r\n`/`\r` → `\n`, and trailing whitespace stripped per line. Text is then split into logical lines: an empty file is zero lines (not one phantom blank line), and a single trailing newline is not treated as an extra blank line — so an empty-vs-content diff reads as a pure addition and a trailing-newline-only change is not reported as a spurious edit. Interior blank lines are preserved. Markdown headings/sections are parsed but are not currently rendered into the report, and never change the text comparison.

14: # Report accessibility & self-containment contract
15: 
16: ## 1. OVERVIEW
17: 
18: The report is meant to be reviewable by everyone, from `file://`, forever, with no dependencies. `scripts/validate_report.py` enforces the safety half of this; the guarantees below describe the whole contract.
19: 
20: ## Self-containment (validated)
21: 
22: - Single HTML file. All CSS is inlined in one `<style>` block; there are no external stylesheets, fonts, scripts, or images.
23: - **Zero JavaScript.** No `<script>` tags and no inline event handlers (`onclick=`, etc.). The report is fully usable with scripting disabled.
24: - **No network.** No remote `href`/`src`. A restrictive Content-Security-Policy meta tag (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`) blocks any accidental request even if the file is opened in a browser.
25: - **Escaped content.** Every piece of source-document text is HTML-escaped, so a document containing markup (or a hostile `<script>`/`onerror=`) is shown as inert text, never executed.
26: 
27: ## Accessibility
28: 
29: - `<html lang="en">`, semantic landmarks (`<header>`, `<main>`, `<section>` with `aria-labelledby`), and a single `<h1>`.
30: - A "Skip to differences" link as the first focusable element.
31: - The change summary is a real `<table>` with row headers (`<th scope="row">`); the diff is a `<table>` with column headers.
32: - **Colour is never the only signal.** Added lines carry a `+`, removed lines a `−`, in a dedicated marker column with an `aria-label` ("added"/"removed"). Word-level changes use `<mark>` with a non-colour decoration in addition to the background tint — inline additions are underlined and inline removals are struck through — so the exact changed substring stays distinguishable for colour-blind users and in monochrome, not only in forced-colours mode.
33: - Contrast targets WCAG AA in both light and dark themes (`prefers-color-scheme`), using `color-scheme: light dark`.
34: - Relative units govern typography and content/column sizing so browser zoom and text scaling work (the 4px spacing scale, hairline borders, and radii use fixed pixel tokens). In the **unified** view, content wraps (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`) so the page itself never scrolls sideways. The **side-by-side** view keeps its two code columns aligned inside a scoped `overflow-x: auto` container that is given a `min-width`, so on a narrow viewport that diff region actually scrolls horizontally instead of collapsing the columns — while the surrounding page (header, summary, legend, footer) still reflows and never forces the whole document to scroll. That scroll container is keyboard-operable: it is a labelled `role="region"` with `tabindex="0"` and a visible focus ring, so a keyboard-only user can focus and scroll it.
35: - Long runs of unchanged lines are collapsed to a labelled "N unchanged lines" row to keep the report scannable.
36: - In validated aggregate reports, every file transition remains visible as a full-width table row group. `START FILE` is the strongest transition, `END FILE` explicitly closes the group, and both include the escaped path as visible text so color is never the only signal. Every file after the first receives a 32px canvas-colored spacer row marked `aria-hidden="true"`; that gap also masks the frame edges at its sides, so it reads as open whitespace without adding empty navigation to the accessibility tree. Boundary rows also reset Markdown section context, preventing a heading from one file from labelling changes in the next.
37: 
38: ## Views
39: 
40: - **Unified** (default): old/new line numbers, a marker column, and content in one column.
41: - **Side-by-side** (`--view side-by-side`): before and after in two columns, each with its own line numbers. The two-column grid is held in a scoped horizontal-scroll region so columns stay aligned rather than wrapping into each other on narrow viewports.
42: 
43: Both views share the same summary, fidelity notes, and legend.
44: 
45: ## What is not guaranteed
46: 
47: The report reflects the extraction tier (see `capabilities-and-fidelity.md`). For `text`/`text*` formats it shows textual change only; it does not claim to show formatting, layout, or tracked-change fidelity, and says so in the "Fidelity notes" section.

18: The report is meant to be reviewable by everyone, from `file://`, forever, with no dependencies. `scripts/validate_report.py` enforces the safety half of this; the guarantees below describe the whole contract.
19: 
20: ## Self-containment (validated)
21: 
22: - Single HTML file. All CSS is inlined in one `<style>` block; there are no external stylesheets, fonts, scripts, or images.
23: - **Zero JavaScript.** No `<script>` tags and no inline event handlers (`onclick=`, etc.). The report is fully usable with scripting disabled.
24: - **No network.** No remote `href`/`src`. A restrictive Content-Security-Policy meta tag (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'`) blocks any accidental request even if the file is opened in a browser.
25: - **Escaped content.** Every piece of source-document text is HTML-escaped, so a document containing markup (or a hostile `<script>`/`onerror=`) is shown as inert text, never executed.
26: 
27: ## Accessibility
28: 
29: - `<html lang="en">`, semantic landmarks (`<header>`, `<main>`, `<section>` with `aria-labelledby`), and a single `<h1>`.
30: - A "Skip to differences" link as the first focusable element.
31: - The change summary is a real `<table>` with row headers (`<th scope="row">`); the diff is a `<table>` with column headers.
32: - **Colour is never the only signal.** Added lines carry a `+`, removed lines a `−`, in a dedicated marker column with an `aria-label` ("added"/"removed"). Word-level changes use `<mark>` with a non-colour decoration in addition to the background tint — inline additions are underlined and inline removals are struck through — so the exact changed substring stays distinguishable for colour-blind users and in monochrome, not only in forced-colours mode.
33: - Contrast targets WCAG AA in both light and dark themes (`prefers-color-scheme`), using `color-scheme: light dark`.
34: - Relative units govern typography and content/column sizing so browser zoom and text scaling work (the 4px spacing scale, hairline borders, and radii use fixed pixel tokens). In the **unified** view, content wraps (`overflow-wrap: anywhere`) so the page itself never scrolls sideways. The **side-by-side** view keeps its two code columns aligned inside a scoped `overflow-x: auto` container that is given a `min-width`, so on a narrow viewport that diff region actually scrolls horizontally instead of collapsing the columns — while the surrounding page (header, summary, legend, footer) still reflows and never forces the whole document to scroll. That scroll container is keyboard-operable: it is a labelled `role="region"` with `tabindex="0"` and a visible focus ring, so a keyboard-only user can focus and scroll it.
35: - Long runs of unchanged lines are collapsed to a labelled "N unchanged lines" row to keep the report scannable.
36: - In validated aggregate reports, every file transition remains visible as a full-width table row group. `START FILE` is the strongest transition, `END FILE` explicitly closes the group, and both include the escaped path as visible text so color is never the only signal. Every file after the first receives a 32px canvas-colored spacer row marked `aria-hidden="true"`; that gap also masks the frame edges at its sides, so it reads as open whitespace without adding empty navigation to the accessibility tree. Boundary rows also reset Markdown section context, preventing a heading from one file from labelling changes in the next.
37: 
38: ## Views
39: 
40: - **Unified** (default): old/new line numbers, a marker column, and content in one column.
41: - **Side-by-side** (`--view side-by-side`): before and after in two columns, each with its own line numbers. The two-column grid is held in a scoped horizontal-scroll region so columns stay aligned rather than wrapping into each other on narrow viewports.
42: 
43: Both views share the same summary, fidelity notes, and legend.
44: 
45: ## What is not guaranteed
46: 
47: The report reflects the extraction tier (see `capabilities-and-fidelity.md`). For `text`/`text*` formats it shows textual change only; it does not claim to show formatting, layout, or tracked-change fidelity, and says so in the "Fidelity notes" section.

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.

206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale

209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting

213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic

219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)

225:             ↓

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible
882: 
883: ---
884: 
885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass
1006: 
1007: ---
1008: 
1009: ## 8. STANDARD STRUCTURE TEMPLATE
1010: 
1011: ### Complete Skill Directory Structure
1012: 
1013: **Path:** `.skilled/skills/` (singular, not `skills` or `openskills`)
1014: 
1015: ```
1016: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
1017: ├── SKILL.md                    # Main skill file (Level 2 in progressive disclosure)
1018: ├── references/                 # Deep-dive technical documentation (Level 3)
1019: │   ├── workflow-name.md        # Multi-phase workflows with checkpoints (kebab-case)
1020: │   ├── patterns-library.md     # Before/after code patterns (kebab-case)
1021: │   ├── debugging-guide.md      # Systematic troubleshooting (kebab-case)
1022: │   └── quick-reference.md      # Commands, shortcuts, checklists (kebab-case)
1023: ├── scripts/                    # Executable Python logic
1024: │   ├── mode_detection.py       # Procedural logic, algorithms
1025: │   ├── workflow_router.py      # Decision logic
1026: │   ├── config_validator.py     # Data transformation
1027: │   └── __init__.py             # Package initialization
1028: ├── assets/                     # Configuration and data files
1029: │   ├── workflow-configs/       # YAML workflow definitions
1030: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
1031: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
1032: │   ├── mappings/               # YAML mapping data
1033: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
1034: │   │   └── mode-recognition.yaml
1035: │   └── templates/              # Markdown/code templates
1036: │       ├── template-name.md
1037: │       └── component-template.tsx
1038: └── tests/                      # Unit and integration tests
1039:     ├── test_mode_detection.py
1040:     ├── test_workflow_router.py
1041:     ├── test_config_validator.py
1042:     └── __init__.py
1043: ```
1044: 
1045: ### Directory Purposes
1046: 
1047: **SKILL.md** (Required): Overview, workflow (3-5 steps), rules. Target: <200 lines
1048: 
1049: **references/** (Optional): Detailed workflows, patterns, debugging. Target: 500-3000 lines/file. **All authored filenames must use kebab-case.**
1050: 
1051: **scripts/** (Optional): Python logic - procedural, routing, validation. Requires type hints, tests
1052: 
1053: **assets/** (Optional): YAML configs, workflow definitions, templates, mappings
1054: 
1055: **tests/** (Required if scripts/ exists): Unit tests with ≥80% coverage, pytest, `test_[name].py`
1056: 
1057: ### When to Create Each Directory
1058: 
1059: | Directory     | Create When                                                     | Don't Create When                           |
1060: | ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
1061: | `references/` | Content >200 lines, multi-phase workflows, systematic debugging | Simple skills <200 lines total              |
1062: | `scripts/`    | Python logic extracted from markdown, reusable functions        | Pure documentation, no executable logic     |
1063: | `assets/`     | YAML configs, templates, structured data                        | No configuration data, inline examples only |
1064: | `tests/`      | `scripts/` directory exists                                     | No Python scripts to test                   |
1065: 
1066: ### Integration Pattern
1067: 
1068: **How components work together:**
1069: - SKILL.md references scripts: `[workflow_router.py](./scripts/workflow_router.py)`
1070: - Scripts load configs: `yaml.safe_load(f"../assets/config.yaml")`
1071: - Tests verify scripts: `assert route_workflow("input").mode == "expected"`
1072: - Markdown links to all: "See [script.py](../scripts/), [config.yaml](../assets/)"

14: # Skill Reference File Templates - AI Agent Skills
15: 
16: Templates for creating reference files in AI agent skills with deep-dive technical guidance.
17: 
18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Location & Naming
23: 
24: **Location:** `.skilled/skills/[skill-name]/references/`
25: 
26: **Naming Convention:** kebab-case with `.md` extension only
27: 
28: | ✅ Valid Names | ❌ Invalid Names |
29: |---------------|-----------------|
30: | `implementation-workflows.md` | `ImplementationWorkflows.md` (PascalCase) |
31: | `tool-catalog.md` | `tool_catalog.md` (snake_case) |
32: | `debugging-guide.md` | `DebuggingGuide.MD` (wrong case) |
33: | `quick-reference.md` | `quickReference.md` (camelCase) |
34: | `code-quality-standards.md` | `code quality standards.md` (spaces) |
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 2. DOCUMENT STRUCTURE
39: 
40: ### Document Structure: Title and Intro
41: 
42: **CRITICAL: The intro after the H1 title must be 1-2 SHORT sentences only.**
43: 
44: ```markdown
45: ---
46: title: [Title]
47: description: [One-line description - same as intro]
48: trigger_phrases:
49:   - "[distinctive phrase one]"
50:   - "[distinctive phrase two]"
51:   - "[distinctive phrase three]"
52: importance_tier: normal
53: contextType: general
54: version: 1.0.0.0
55: ---
56: 
57: # [Title]
58: 
59: [1-2 SHORT sentences only. Brief hook/summary. NO subsections, NO headers here.]
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: \## 1. OVERVIEW
64: [All detailed content goes here, NOT in the intro]
65: 
66: ```
67: 
68: Every reference file carries this full 5-field frontmatter block: the Skill Advisor harvests it as routing signal (3-8 lowercase multi-word `trigger_phrases` drawn from the doc's content. `importance_tier` defaults to `normal`, with `important` only for formal contract docs. `contextType` is one of `planning|research|implementation|general`). See [frontmatter-templates.md](../../../sk-create-frontmatter/assets/frontmatter-templates.md) for field rules.
69: 
70: > **WARNING: DO NOT duplicate content between intro and Section 1.**
71: > The intro is a hook. Section 1 provides the details.
72: 
73: #### GOOD Intro Structure
74: 
75: ```markdown
76: # Git Commit Workflows
77: 
78: This reference turns a mixed working tree into a small set of reviewable commits.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: \## 1. OVERVIEW
83: 
84: ### Purpose
85: Each rule keeps one commit focused on one intent, so history stays easy to read, review and revert.
86: 
87: ### When to Use
88: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
89: - Filtering generated files from commits
90: - Writing clear commit messages
91: 
92: ### Core Principle
93: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
94: ```
95: 
96: #### BAD Intro Structure (duplicates content)
97: 
98: ```markdown
99: # Git Commit Workflows
100: 
101: Step-by-step workflows for creating clean, atomic commits with proper filtering.
102: 
103: ### Core Principle   ← WRONG: No headers in intro!
104: Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history.
105: 
106: ### When to Use      ← WRONG: This belongs in Section 1!
107: - Creating commits with multiple file changes
108: 
109: ---
110: 
111: \## 1. OVERVIEW
112: 
113: ### Purpose
114: Provides systematic workflows...  ← Now this duplicates the intro!
115: 
116: ### Core Principle
117: Atomic commits...  ← DUPLICATED from intro!
118: ```
119: 
120: #### Intro vs Section 1 Content Placement
121: 
122: | Content Type          | Intro (after H1) | Section 1 OVERVIEW |
123: | --------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------ |
124: | 1-2 sentence summary  | ✅ YES            | ❌ NO (don't repeat) |
125: | Core Principle        | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
126: | When to Use           | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
127: | Primary Sources       | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES (as "Key Sources") |
128: | Purpose (detailed)    | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
129: | Prerequisites         | ❌ NO             | ✅ YES              |
130: | Any H3 subsections    | ❌ NEVER          | ✅ YES              |
131: 
132: ---
133: 
134: ### Reference Body Skeleton
135: 
136: **Every reference body follows this order.** The hook and the Purpose say different things: the hook names the job, and the Purpose names the outcome.
137: 
138: ```markdown
139: # [Title]
140: 
141: [1-2 sentence hook: what this reference covers and when to reach for it.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## 1. OVERVIEW
146: 
147: ### Purpose
148: 
149: [The outcome this reference produces, in one or two sentences.]
150: 
151: ### When to Use
152: 
153: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
154: - [Second trigger]
155: 
156: ### Core Principle
157: 
158: [One-line statement that governs every rule below.]
159: 
160: ### Boundaries
161: 
162: - **In scope**: [What this reference owns]
163: - **Out of scope**: [What belongs in a sibling reference]
164: 
165: ### Key Sources
166: 
167: - [title](url) - [What the source establishes]
168: 
169: ---
170: 
171: ## 2. [CONTENT SECTION]
172: 
173: ### [Rule Group]
174: 
175: - **Rule:** [What to do]
176: - **Why:** [The failure it prevents]
177: - **Check:** [How to verify it]
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## 3. [CONTENT SECTION]
182: 
183: [Body of the section]
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## 4. RELATED RESOURCES
188: 
189: - [title](./sibling-reference.md) - [What the reader gets there]
190: ```
191: 
192: **Rules the skeleton encodes:**
193: - Core Principle, Boundaries and Key Sources follow Purpose and When to Use, in that order, and each appears only when it has content.
194: - Content sections use integer numbers only: `## 2.`, `## 3.`, and so on.
195: - Rule fields are `- **Label:** text` bullets, never two bold labels on consecutive lines.
196: - Links are `[title](url)`, never a bare URL.
197: - Every `---` has a blank line above it, so a divider never turns the line above into a setext heading.
198: - A related section, when present, is the last H2.

202: ### What Are AI Agent Skill Reference Files?
203: 
204: Reference files are detailed technical documentation in the `references/` directory that provide deep-dive guidance with **explicit reasoning** - making thought processes visible, showing decision logic, and analyzing root causes.
205: 
206: **Core Purpose**:
207: - **Technical depth** - Step-by-step reasoning with rationale
208: - **Phased workflows** - Structured processes with validation checkpoints
209: - **Pattern libraries** - Before/after examples, comparison tables
210: - **Tool integration** - MCP tools, scripts, asset references
211: - **Root cause analysis** - Systematic debugging and troubleshooting
212: 
213: **Key Difference from Generic Documentation**:
214: - AI agent skills = Actionable workflows with explicit reasoning
215: - Generic docs = Information reference without decision logic
216: 
217: ### Progressive Disclosure in Skills
218: 
219: ```
220: Level 1: Metadata (name + description)
221:          └─ Always in context (~100 words)
222:             ↓
223: Level 2: SKILL.md body
224:          └─ When skill triggers (<5k words)
225:             ↓
226: Level 3: Reference files (this document)
227:          └─ Loaded as needed (500-3000 lines per file)
228: ```
229: 
230: **Reference files = Level 3**: Deep technical guidance loaded only when the agent needs specific workflow details.
231: 
232: ---

234: ## 3. WHEN TO CREATE REFERENCE FILES

236: ### Create Reference File When
237: 
238: **Workflow Complexity**:
239: - Multi-phase workflows with validation checkpoints
240: - Decision trees with multiple branches
241: - Pattern libraries with 5+ variations
242: - Systematic debugging procedures
243: 
244: **Technical Depth**:
245: - Root cause analysis required
246: - Tool integration details (MCP, scripts)
247: - Before/after code transformations
248: - Common error patterns and fixes
249: 
250: **Size Threshold**:
251: - Content exceeds 200 lines
252: - Multiple related workflows
253: - Extensive troubleshooting needed
254: 
255: ### Keep in SKILL.md When
256: 
257: **Core Content**:
258: - Overview and "When to Use"
259: - High-level workflow (3-5 steps)
260: - Essential rules (ALWAYS/NEVER/ESCALATE IF)

262: - Quick reference

264: **Size**: Content under 200 lines

281: ## 4. AI AGENT SKILL REFERENCE CHARACTERISTICS
282: 
283: ### Core Principle Statements
284: 
285: **Purpose**: Distill philosophy into one-line wisdom
286: 
287: > **PLACEMENT**: Core Principle goes in **Section 1 OVERVIEW**, NOT in the intro paragraph after the H1 title.
288: 
289: **Format**:
290: ```markdown
291: \## 1. OVERVIEW
292: 
293: ### Purpose
294: 
295: [The outcome this reference produces]
296: 
297: ### When to Use
298: 
299: - [Trigger that sends a reader here]
300: 
301: ### Core Principle
302: 
303: [Single powerful statement that captures the workflow's essence]
304: ```

306: **Examples from Real Skills**:
307: - "Wait for the actual condition you care about, not a guess about how long it takes"
308: - "ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure"
309: - "Atomic commits with clear intent + filtered artifacts = maintainable Git history"
310: 
311: ### Phased Workflows with Validation
312: 
313: **Purpose**: Structured processes with mandatory checkpoints
314: 
315: **Format**:
316: ```markdown
317: ### The [Number] Phases
318: 
319: You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

322:

326: 1. [Action 1]
327: 2. [Action 2]
328: 
329: **Validation**: `checkpoint_name`

336: **Key Elements**:
337: - **"You MUST complete"** - Mandatory language

342: 
343: **Purpose**: Show transformation from wrong to right

346: ```markdown

348:

359: \```

362: ```
363: 
364: **Key Elements**:
365: - `BEFORE:` marker for the wrong-way code
366: - `AFTER:` marker for the right-way code
367: - Inline comments explaining issues

381: | [Scenario 2] | [Wrong way]        | [Right way]        | [Rationale] |
382: ```
383: 
384: **Use when**: Multiple scenarios need comparison

682: ## 5. CONVERTING LOGIC TO EXECUTABLE CODE
683: 
684: ### When to Extract Logic from Markdown
685: 
686: **Purpose**: Separate documentation from executable code for better maintainability, testability, and reusability.
687: 
688: **Decision Criteria**:
689: 
690: | Pattern Type          | Keep in Markdown  | Extract to Code           | Reasoning                                    |
691: | --------------------- | ----------------- | ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
692: | **Python functions**  | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/scripts/*.py`   | Type safety, unit testing, reusability       |
693: | **YAML configs**      | ❌ No              | ✅ Yes → `/assets/*.yaml`  | Dynamic loading, version control, validation |
694: | **Decision trees**    | ⚠️ High-level only | ✅ Details → YAML + Python | Machine-readable, can be validated           |
695: | **Command mappings**  | ⚠️ Examples only   | ✅ Full map → YAML         | Easier maintenance, can be imported          |
696: | **Workflow diagrams** | ✅ Yes (generated) | ✅ Source → YAML           | YAML = source of truth, diagram = output     |
697: | **Checklists**        | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Human-readable is primary use case           |
698: | **Before/after code** | ✅ Yes             | ❌ No                      | Educational, not executable                  |
699: 
700: ### Extraction Pattern
701: 
702: **In Markdown (Reference File)**:
703: ```markdown
704: ### [Workflow Name]
705: 
706: [High-level description of what the workflow does]
707: 
708: **Implementation:** See [workflow_name.py](../scripts/workflow_name.py) for execution logic and [workflow-config.yaml](../assets/workflow-config.yaml) for configuration.
709: 
710: **Quick Overview**:
711: 1. [Step 1 - high level]
712: 2. [Step 2 - high level]
713: 3. [Step 3 - high level]
714: 
715: **Configuration Options:**
716: - See YAML config for customizable parameters
717: - Default values optimized for common use cases
718: ```
719: 
720: ### Benefits of Separation
721: 
722: - **Type safety** - Python type hints catch errors at development time
723: - **Testability** - Unit tests for logic, integration tests for workflows
724: - **Reusability** - Imported by multiple skills or scripts
725: - **Version control** - Git diffs show logic changes clearly
726: - **Schema validation** - YAML can be validated against schemas
727: - **Dynamic loading** - Configuration changes without code edits
728: 
729: ### Example: Mode Detection Extraction
730: 
731: **❌ BEFORE** (inline Python in markdown):
732: \```python
733: def detect_mode(request):
734:     if '$quick' in request: return 'quick', 5
735:     elif '$ticket' in request: return 'ticket', 10
736:     return 'interactive', 10
737: \```
738: 
739: **✅ AFTER** (extracted with type safety):
740: 
741: `/scripts/mode_detection.py`:
742: \```python
743: from dataclasses import dataclass
744: 
745: @dataclass
746: class ModeConfig:
747:     mode: str
748:     depth_rounds: int
749: 
750: def detect_mode(request: str) -> ModeConfig:
751:     """Detect mode from command shortcuts."""
752:     if '$quick' in request:
753:         return ModeConfig('quick', 5)
754:     elif '$ticket' in request:
755:         return ModeConfig('ticket', 10)
756:     return ModeConfig('interactive', 10)
757: \```
758: 
759: `/tests/test_mode_detection.py`:
760: \```python
761: def test_quick_mode():
762:     assert detect_mode("$quick fix").mode == 'quick'
763: \```
764: 
765: **Why better:** Type hints, testable, reusable, separated from docs
766:

769: ## 6. YAML CONFIGURATION PATTERNS
770: 
771: ### Purpose
772: 
773: **YAML for configuration data** - Separate configuration from documentation for easier maintenance and dynamic loading.
774: 
775: **When to use YAML**:
776: - Configuration data (thresholds, mappings, rules)
777: - Data structures (nested objects, lists)
778: - Workflow definitions (step sequences, pipelines)
779: - Decision trees (conditional logic patterns)
780: - Validation schemas
781: 
782: ### Standard YAML Structure
783: 
784: ```yaml
785: # [config-name].yaml
786: metadata:
787:   version: "1.0.0"
788:   description: "Configuration for [feature name]"
789: 
790: config:
791:   threshold_values:
792:     low: 1
793:     medium: 5
794:     high: 10
795:   feature_flags:
796:     enable_feature_x: true
797:   mappings:
798:     $quick: "quick_mode"
799:     $ticket: "ticket_mode"
800: ```
801: 
802: ### File Organization
803: 
804: ```
805: .skilled/skills/[skill-name]/
806: ├── assets/
807: │   ├── workflow-configs/
808: │   │   ├── canvas-methodology.yaml
809: │   │   ├── variant-detection.yaml
810: │   │   └── complexity-scoring.yaml
811: │   ├── mappings/
812: │   │   ├── command-mappings.yaml
813: │   │   ├── mode-recognition.yaml
814: │   │   └── shortcut-definitions.yaml
815: │   └── templates/
816: │       └── [template files]
817: ```
818: 
819: ### Loading Pattern (Python)
820: 
821: ```python
822: import yaml
823: from pathlib import Path
824: 
825: def load_config(config_name: str) -> dict:
826:     """Load YAML config from assets directory."""
827:     config_path = Path(__file__).parent.parent / f"assets/{config_name}.yaml"
828:     with open(config_path) as f:
829:         return yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
830: 
831: # Usage
832: config = load_config("canvas-methodology")
833: ```
834: 
835: ### Example: Variant Detection Rules
836: 
837: **❌ BEFORE** (markdown table):
838: ```markdown
839: | Trigger                    | Action             |
840: | -------------------------- | ------------------ |
841: | "show options"             | Offer 3-5 variants |
842: | Complexity 7+ + "not sure" | Offer variants     |
843: ```
844: 
845: **✅ AFTER** (YAML + Python):
846: 
847: `/assets/variant-detection-rules.yaml`:
848: ```yaml
849: config:
850:   variant_triggers:
851:     explicit_keywords: ["show me options", "variations"]
852:     implicit:
853:       complexity_threshold: 7
854:       uncertainty_signals: ["not sure", "what would work"]
855:   variant_count:
856:     simple: [2, 3]
857:     complex: [5, 10]
858: ```
859: 
860: `/scripts/variant_detector.py`:
861: ```python
862: import yaml
863: 
864: class VariantDetector:
865:     def __init__(self, config_path: str):
866:         with open(config_path) as f:
867:             self.config = yaml.safe_load(f)['config']
868: 
869:     def should_generate_variants(self, request: str, complexity: int) -> bool:
870:         keywords = self.config['variant_triggers']['explicit_keywords']
871:         if any(kw in request.lower() for kw in keywords):
872:             return True
873: 
874:         threshold = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['complexity_threshold']
875:         if complexity >= threshold:
876:             signals = self.config['variant_triggers']['implicit']['uncertainty_signals']
877:             return any(s in request.lower() for s in signals)
878:         return False
879: ```
880: 
881: **Why better:** Dynamic config loading, easier maintenance, schema validation possible

885: ## 7. PYTHON SCRIPT INTEGRATION
886: 
887: ### When to Use Python for Logic
888: 
889: **Use Python scripts when**:
890: - Procedural logic (workflows, algorithms)
891: - Complex conditionals (multi-step decisions)
892: - Data transformation (processing, validation)
893: - API integration (external services)
894: - File operations (reading, parsing, generating)
895: 
896: ### Type Hints and Docstring Standards
897: 
898: **Always include**:
899: - Type hints for parameters and return values
900: - Google-style docstrings (Args, Returns, Raises, Examples)
901: - Dataclasses for structured data
902: 
903: **Example**:
904: ```python
905: from dataclasses import dataclass
906: from pathlib import Path
907: 
908: @dataclass
909: class ValidationResult:
910:     is_valid: bool
911:     errors: list[str]
912: 
913: def validate_config(config_path: Path) -> ValidationResult:
914:     """
915:     Validate configuration file.
916: 
917:     Args:
918:         config_path: Path to YAML config file
919: 
920:     Returns:
921:         ValidationResult with status and errors
922: 
923:     Raises:
924:         FileNotFoundError: If config doesn't exist
925:     """
926:     if not config_path.exists():
927:         raise FileNotFoundError(f"Config not found: {config_path}")
928:     # Validation logic
929:     return ValidationResult(is_valid=True, errors=[])
930: ```
931: 
932: ### Unit Testing Requirements
933: 
934: **Every Python script must have tests**:
935: - Naming: `test_[script_name].py` in `/tests/` directory
936: - Coverage: ≥80% line coverage
937: - Framework: pytest
938: 
939: **Example**:
940: ```python
941: import pytest
942: from scripts.config_validator import validate_config
943: 
944: def test_validate_success(tmp_path):
945:     config = tmp_path / "config.yaml"
946:     config.write_text("config:\n  threshold: 5")
947:     result = validate_config(config)
948:     assert result.is_valid
949: 
950: def test_validate_missing_file():
951:     with pytest.raises(FileNotFoundError):
952:         validate_config(Path("nonexistent.yaml"))
953: ```
954: 
955: ### Import and Reference Patterns
956: 
957: **Python import order**: Standard library → Third-party → Local
958: 
959: **Markdown references**:
960: ```markdown
961: **See also:** [script_name.py](../scripts/script_name.py), [config.yaml](../assets/config.yaml)
962: ```
963: 
964: ### Example: Workflow Decision Logic
965: 
966: **❌ BEFORE** (text decision tree):
967: ```markdown
968: IF "$quick": use quick mode (5 rounds)
969: IF "$ticket": use ticket mode (10 rounds)
970: OTHERWISE: use interactive mode
971: ```
972: 
973: **✅ AFTER** (Python with type safety):
974: 
975: `/scripts/workflow_router.py`:
976: ```python
977: from typing import Literal
978: from dataclasses import dataclass
979: 
980: WorkflowMode = Literal["quick", "ticket", "interactive"]
981: 
982: @dataclass
983: class WorkflowDecision:
984:     mode: WorkflowMode
985:     depth_rounds: int
986: 
987: def route_workflow(request: str) -> WorkflowDecision:
988:     """Route request to appropriate workflow."""
989:     if '$quick' in request.lower():
990:         return WorkflowDecision("quick", 5)
991:     if '$ticket' in request.lower():
992:         return WorkflowDecision("ticket", 10)
993:     return WorkflowDecision("interactive", 10)
994: ```
995: 
996: `/tests/test_workflow_router.py`:
997: ```python
998: def test_quick_mode():
999:     assert route_workflow("$quick fix").mode == "quick"
1000: 
1001: def test_default_mode():
1002:     assert route_workflow("help me").mode == "interactive"
1003: ```
1004: 
1005: **Why better:** Type-safe with Literal, testable, structured with dataclass

14: # SKILL.md File Templates - Creation Guide
15: 
16: Templates for creating SKILL.md files with proper structure, frontmatter, and required sections.

18: ---
19: 
20: ## 1. OVERVIEW
21: 
22: ### Purpose of SKILL.md Files
23: 
24: SKILL.md files define AI agent skills - reusable capabilities that extend an agent's functionality for specific domains or workflows. A well-crafted SKILL.md:
25: 
26: - **Triggers automatically** when relevant patterns are detected
27: - **Guides the agent** through specialized workflows
28: - **Maintains consistency** across conversations
29: - **Encodes expertise** in specific domains
30: 
31: ### Template Overview
32: 
33: This guide provides **one comprehensive SKILL template** (Section 3) that covers all skill types from simple single-purpose tools to complex multi-mode orchestrators.
34: 
35: **The template is flexible:**
36: - **Simple skills**: Use required core sections only (WHEN TO USE, SMART ROUTING, HOW IT WORKS, RULES, REFERENCES)
37: - **Skills with bundled resources**: Say in Section 2 what selects the skill and what it loads first, and put the router in the sibling `ROUTER.md`. Use `references/`, `assets/`, and `scripts/`
38: - **Multi-mode skills**: Expand WHEN TO USE and HOW IT WORKS sections by mode
39: - **All skills**: Section 2 (SMART ROUTING) is required: 8 to 12 non-blank lines of plain prose
40: 
41: **Target size**: 800-2000 lines for SKILL.md (<5k words total)
42: 
43: **Examples**:
44: - Simple: Unit test generator, documentation formatter (no bundled resources)
45: - Moderate: API client, specialized code reviewer (with references and assets)
46: - Complex: Workflow orchestrator, document quality pipeline (multi-mode with extensive resources)
47: 
48: ### Progressive Disclosure Principle
49: 
50: SKILL.md architecture follows progressive disclosure:
51: 
52: 1. **Metadata** (YAML frontmatter) - Always in context (~100 words)
53: 2. **SKILL.md body** - When skill activates (<5k words)
54: 3. **Bundled resources** - Loaded as needed (unlimited size)
55: 
56: **Critical**: Keep SKILL.md <5k words. Move detailed content to `references/`, `scripts/`, or `assets/`.
57: 
58: ### Document Type Requirements
59: 
60: **Enforcement Level**: STRICT (SKILL.md files require perfect structure)
61: 
62: **Required Elements**:
63: - ✅ YAML frontmatter with required fields
64: - ✅ H1 title with subtitle
65: - ✅ Numbered H2 sections (ALL CAPS, integers only, never a letter suffix such as `2b.`)
66: - ✅ Section separators (`---`)
67: - ✅ No table of contents (forbidden in SKILL.md)

503: 
504: ### Section 2: SMART ROUTING (Required for All Skills)
505: 
506: **Purpose**: Use this section to explain how you route a request to this skill's resources.
507: 
508: **Three skill kinds, one shape**:
509: 
510: | Kind | How to tell | What Section 2 says |
511: |------|-------------|---------------------|
512: | Hub | the folder holds `mode-registry.json` and `hub-router.json` | how a prompt reaches a mode, and where the root `ROUTER.md` is |
513: | Mode packet | a packet folder inside a hub | what selects this packet, what it loads first, and where its own `ROUTER.md` is |
514: | Standalone | neither hub file | the same as a mode packet, with the router in its own `ROUTER.md` |
515: 
516: **The limit**: 12 non-blank lines and 180 words are the hard ceilings the check enforces. Aim for 8 to 12 lines. A packet or standalone skill says three things: what selects it, what it loads first, and where the machine router is.
517: 
518: **The sibling router**: the machine router lives in `ROUTER.md` beside `SKILL.md`, under a final `## MACHINE ROUTER` heading.
519: That heading is the one every reader parses. Its section number is optional, so `## MACHINE ROUTER` and `## 9. MACHINE ROUTER` both count, and the check ignores the number.
520: Keep pseudocode out of SMART ROUTING and put it in that section.
521: `SKILL.md` carries no `## MACHINE ROUTER` section of its own: two homes for one router is the dual declaration the check reports.
522: 
523: **The link line**: Section 2 names the router file with a relative markdown link, [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md), and its target resolves on disk. A sentence that mentions the name without a link fails, because a reader cannot follow it to a file that is not there.
524: 
525: **One router per folder**: every skill and every mode packet owns `ROUTER.md` inside its own folder, linked from its own `SKILL.md`. A router file whose real path leaves the folder is not that skill's router.
526: 
527: **The no-match outcome** is named `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` everywhere. Low confidence returns a disambiguation checklist, never an empty result and never a guess.
528: 
529: **Validation**: `package_skill.py --strict` reports the routing shape with five codes:
530: 
531: | Code | Finding |
532: |------|---------|
533: | `RS-001` | SMART ROUTING is longer than the limit (12 lines or 180 words by default) |
534: | `RS-002` | `SKILL.md` carries a `## MACHINE ROUTER` section, with or without a code block |
535: | `RS-003` | A `## MACHINE ROUTER` section is not the last H2 of the document that holds it |
536: | `RS-004` | the skill has no sibling `ROUTER.md`, or its real path leaves the skill folder |
537: | `RS-005` | `SKILL.md` has no relative markdown link to `./ROUTER.md` that resolves |
538: 
539: The machine block itself is a fenced block or an unfenced run of indented lines.
540: It declares the router with one of these markers: `INTENT_SIGNALS =`, `RESOURCE_MAP =`, `DEFAULT_RESOURCE =`, `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST =`, `def discover_markdown_resources` or `def _guard_in_skill`.
541: A fence closes only on a run of the same character that is at least as long as its opening run.
542: 
543: **Known debt** is listed in `sk-create-skill/scripts/routing-shape-known-debt.json`.
544: Entries use skill paths relative to `.skilled/skills`, such as `sk-code/sk-code-review`.
545: A folder outside that root is never debt.
546: Each entry records `{"lines", "words", "machineBlocks", "codes"}`.
547: A listed skill fails if its line count, word count or machine blocks left in `SKILL.md` exceed the record, or if it adds an unrecorded code.
548: The checker ignores entries in any other form.
549: Remove an entry when the skill follows the canon.
550: 
551: **Placement**: the SMART ROUTING section sits after Section 1 (WHEN TO USE) and before HOW IT WORKS, and `ROUTER.md` sits beside `SKILL.md` at the skill root.
552: 
553: **Worked example** (a canon Section 2 and its sibling router, nothing else):
554: 
555: \## 2. SMART ROUTING
556: 
557: Use this skill for [domain] work: [trigger 1], [trigger 2], or [trigger 3].
558: The first signal is [project/stack/mode detection], because it picks the knowledge folder before any intent scoring.
559: Load `references/[default].md` first on every run. The other files assume it.
560: Then load what the matched intent maps to: [intent A] reads `references/[domain]/[a].md`, and [intent B] reads `assets/[domain]/[b].md`.
561: Keep every path inside this skill folder and load a file only when it exists.
562: When two intents score close together, follow both in rank order.
563: When nothing matches, report `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` with the checklist from the machine router instead of guessing.
564: The machine router lives in [`ROUTER.md`](./ROUTER.md); read it before selecting a resource.
565: 
566: ---
567: 
568: The link resolves to the sibling file, whose one heading the readers parse is:
569: 
570: \## MACHINE ROUTER
571: 
572: ```python
573: DEFAULT_RESOURCE = "references/[default].md"
574: INTENT_SIGNALS = {"PRIMARY": {"weight": 4, "keywords": [("[keyword]", 4), ("[phrase]", 3)]}}
575: RESOURCE_MAP = {"PRIMARY": ["references/[domain]/[primary].md"]}
576: UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST = ["Confirm the routing key", "Confirm the intent", "Provide one concrete input"]
577: 
578: def route_[skill_name]_resources(user_request, task=None):
579:     inventory = discover_markdown_resources()
580:     primary, secondary, scores = classify_intents(user_request, task)
581:     if max(scores.values() or [0]) < 0.5:
582:         return {"load_level": "UNKNOWN_FALLBACK", "checklist": UNKNOWN_FALLBACK_CHECKLIST}
583:     return {"routing_key": get_routing_key(task, [primary]), "resources": inventory}
584: ```
585: 
586: The full resilience pattern (guarded paths, recursive discovery, routing keys) is in [skill-smart-router.md](./skill-smart-router.md).
587: 
588: **Writing Tips**:
589: - Open Section 2 with the signal that actually picks this skill's files.
590: - Name the first file to load, so a reader knows where to start.
591: - Name the router file with a markdown link, so a reader can open it.
592: - Keep `UNKNOWN_FALLBACK` as the named no-match outcome.
593: - Edit `INTENT_SIGNALS` and `RESOURCE_MAP` in `ROUTER.md` when the skill gains a domain.
594: - Avoid duplicate lookup tables, static file inventories, and unguarded `load()` calls.
595: 
596: **Word Budget**: 8-12 non-blank lines of prose
